sections.title: 0. Changes from the Previous Edition
sections.html:
This 8-K is not a new event but the closing record of an event already settled. It discloses that the five series of yen-denominated senior notes, whose terms were set on 2026-11-13 (FWP), were actually issued on 2026-11-19, and attaches the underlying agreements (underwriting agreement, officer's certificate, legal opinion) as evidence. Principal, coupon and maturity are the same as in the FWP and 424B5 — T8 stays 'confirmed' and only settlement completed is added. The Form 4 on the same measurement-layer list (director Charlotte Guyman, gift of 400 Class B shares) does not affect the company. The Buffett Thanksgiving press release (2026-11-16), which the previous edition could not read, was read in full this time — the figures match 13D/A No. 82. Probabilities and assumed value band do not move — no rule has been met.

Source: the 8-K above. Terms cross-check: FWP 2026-11-13 · 424B5 final prospectus supplement — principal, coupon and maturity are identical for all five series.

  • Contract structure (8-K text): issued under shelf registration statement S-3 (No. 333-284622, 2025-01-31) · underwriting agreement 2026-11-13 (Mizuho Securities USA · Merrill Lynch International) · indenture 2025-01-31 (Berkshire · Berkshire Hathaway Finance Corporation · The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company) · five officer's certificates, one per series, and a Baker & McKenzie legal opinion (all 2026-11-19, source: 8-K exhibit list).
  • New numbers the 8-K gives: none. The only thing newly confirmed is that the settlement that had been 'scheduled' actually took place (judgment). The date given as 'settlement scheduled 2026-11-19' in the previous two installments was correct (cross-check: 424B5 scheduled settlement date ↔ 8-K issue date).
  • What the 8-K does not give: the redemption of the notes to be refinanced — ¥73.4 billion (0.955%, maturing 2026-11-27) and ¥23.0 billion (0.203%, maturing 2027-01-25). The use of proceeds is stated in the 424B5 (source: 424B5), and redemption is to be confirmed after the maturity dates, in the 4Q26 10-K debt footnote.
How large this issuance is relative to Berkshire's numbers (rough)
  • Dollar conversion: ¥182.3 billion ÷ 159.97 ≈ $1.14 billion (estimate — the yen/dollar rate is 159.97, ECB as of 2026-11-19 per data/fx_lens.json). Net increase excluding the refinanced portion: ¥85.9 billion (formula 1,823 − 964) ≈ $0.54 billion (estimate, same rate — the ¥96.4 billion of refinanced notes is from the 424B5).
  • Annual interest cost: new notes about ¥5.42 billion (formula Σ principal × coupon = 24.14 + 17.23 + 5.33 + 0.99 + 6.49) vs refinanced notes about ¥0.75 billion (formula 734 × 0.955% + 230 × 0.203%) → difference about ¥4.67 billion ≈ $29 million per year (pre-tax, estimate — same rate. Principal and coupons from the 8-K and 424B5).
  • Comparison: about 0.2% (formula 29 ÷ 12,705, ignoring the pre-tax/after-tax difference) of 3Q26 one-quarter after-tax operating earnings of $12.705 billion (source: 8-K EX-99.1) — the size that reaches the earnings engine is small (judgment). Against the headline cash of $377.4 billion, the net increase of $0.54 billion is about 0.1% (formula 5.4 ÷ 3,774).
  • Interpretation (judgment): it is common to explain yen-denominated notes as a pairing with the currency exposure of the Japanese trading-house stakes (yen assets), but the 8-K and 424B5 this probe read do not state such a purpose (the 424B5 use-of-proceeds section explicitly names refinancing) — a hedging purpose could not be confirmed from the original text. That coupons are about 2 percentage points higher than the previous generation (0.2–1.0%) is an observation showing a change in the Japanese interest rate level (formula 2.97% − 0.955%, source: 424B5).

Buffett and NoVo 1,845,000 shares each) · after the donation 182,140 Class A shares and 1,162 Class B shares. Not a single figure differs from 13D/A No. 82 in the previous issue (cross-check: 13D/A No. 82).
  • Buffett's statement in the press release — to the effect that he plans to donate all of his Berkshire shares to the four foundations — is recorded only as a milestone candidate under Rule 1 of the protocol (state.manager_statements_as_milestone_candidates_only). It is not used as a basis for judgment. If this statement comes true, the 29.6% voting power (No. 82) would shift toward the foundations over time or be diluted by Class B conversion — an observation target for Axis E, but since no timing is set, it is not made a milestone (judgment, sources: press release · 13D/A No. 82).
  • Form 4 (source: Form 4, signed 2026-11-19): director Charlotte Guyman gifted 400 Class B shares on 2026-11-17 (code G, price $0), leaving 2,488 Class B shares held directly after the transaction. It is unrelated to the company's equity and share count (judgment).

sections.html:
• Axis C (capital allocation): the net borrowing increase of about $540 million (estimate) moves both the numerator and denominator of C-2027-1 (cash ÷ total assets ≤25%) by nearly the same amount — the judged figure of 28.9% (9/30, 10-Q) is a quarterly figure, so it is not re-measured this issue.
  • No change in judgment for all 14 milestones — this disclosure provides no new measurement unit (quarterly earnings, balance sheet, annual transactions). One 'in progress' line is appended to each status_history (disclosure contents: only Items 8.01 and 9.01 of the 8-K).
  • Among rules R1–R6, none is conditioned on borrowing (source: state.probability_adjustment_rules · rule definitions in the [2026-11 report](2026-11.md)).

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.html:
• One-sentence conclusion: The 2026-11-19 8-K is a record of the completed issuance of five series of yen notes (¥182.3 billion, weighted coupon 2.97%) that were finalized on 11-13, and it gives no new figures — the net increase of about $540 million and the annual interest increase of about $29 million (estimate) are too small to reach earnings or cash, and the 25/50/25 probabilities and the assumed value are unchanged (source: 8-K).
  • Briefing in 5 lines
  • 8-K (2026-11-19): issuance of five series of yen senior notes completed — ¥92.0 billion 2.624% 2029 · ¥57.3 billion 3.007% 2031 · ¥16.1 billion 3.313% 2033 · ¥2.7 billion 3.661% 2036 · ¥14.2 billion 4.571% 2056 (8-K).
  • Terms are the same as the FWP (11-13) and 424B5 (11-17 EDGAR) — T8 stays confirmed; only settlement completion is added.
  • Net increase of ¥85.9 billion (about $540 million, yen/dollar 159.97, estimate) versus the ¥96.4 billion to be refinanced · annual interest increase of about ¥4.67 billion (formula).
  • Reading of Buffett's Thanksgiving press release (11-16) — the conversion and donation figures match 13D/A No. 82 (press release).
  • No rule R1–R6 met — scenarios 25/50/25 and assumed value band $265.0–$684.5 maintained · Class B 11/19 close $572.04 (P/B 1.60x) (stockanalysis).
  • Three data points to check directly before the next issue
  • Repayment of the ¥73.4 billion (0.955%, maturing 2026-11-27) to be refinanced — 4Q26 10-K debt note (T2, 424B5).
  • Whether Bending Spoons' 6.4% stake as of 9/30 is the figure after settlement of the additional shares (T5, 13G).
  • Whether Delta's stake crosses from 9.8% to 10% — 13G amendment · Form 4 (T3, Delta 13G).
